title: Schema Governor & Deferred Tool Execution: Acceptance + Operator Playbook
creator: Evelyn Park
description: Define pragmatic acceptance criteria and operational runbook for: (1) schema arbitration when models emit typed/partial frames, (2) deferred tool/function execution semantics (idempotency, retries, and backpressure), and (3) streaming checkpoints and soft-fail modes. Goal is a testable contract that balances developer ergonomics with production reliability and operator clarity.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Schema handshake: For any streaming session where a typed frame is expected, the runtime must accept an initial 'schema-offer' frame or fail with a documented error code (TOOL_SCHEMA_MISMATCH). 2) Deterministic framing: Partial objects (fragments) must include sequence_id and commit markers; client can reassemble in order or receive an explicit missing-fragment error. 3) Checkpointing: The emitter MUST produce optional checkpoint frames at configurable intervals (default every 4s or 512 tokens) that include a stable cursor for resumption. 4) Deferred execute semantics: If model emits 'defer_tool_call' with tool payload_id, Redwood must persist a durable call intent with idempotency_token and either execute within configured window (default 30s) or surface a deferred status to client. 5) Idempotency: Every tool call initiated by the runtime must include an idempotency_token; duplicate requests must be deduplicated server-side. 6) Backpressure & soft-fail: If target tool is overloaded, the runtime must attempt N=3 exponential retries with jitter; if still failing, runtime must return a soft-fail envelope that contains partial data plus a standardized failure_reason and recommended next steps. 7) Observable telemetry: Each stream must emit metrics: frames_emitted, fragments_committed, tool_calls_attempted, tool_calls_succeeded, tool_calls_failed_{class}, checkpoint_latency_ms. 8) E2E tests: For each acceptance flow there are passing E2E scenarios (happy path, partial-fragment loss, tool-timeout, schema-mismatch) — see test_plan. 9) Backwards compatibility: Old clients (no schema-offer) must still succeed under best-effort mode with a warning frame; no silent silent-swallowing of tool-calls for older clients. 10) Security: Deferred tool payloads must be encrypted at rest and KMS-access controlled in Private deployments.
decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Chose schema-offer handshake (model->runtime) instead of runtime-driven schema negotiation to minimize round-trips and keep streaming latency low. Trade-off: some older clients will operate in best-effort mode and receive warning frames.
- Checkpoint cadence is a configurable knob; default tuned for low-latency chat use-cases. Faster checkpoints increase durability but add overhead.
- Deferred execution stored as durable intent in runtime DB (small write) vs synchronous broker call — durable intent simplifies retries and observability but requires migration work for Dedicated/Private.
- Soft-fail envelope preferred to hard abort to preserve graceful degradation for user-facing apps. This requires clear guidance to SDKs to present partial results and suggested remediation.
implementation_notes:
Engineering tasks: 1) runtime: implement schema-offer frame parsing, fragment ordering keys, and checkpoint emission API. 2) persistence: store deferred tool intents with idempotency_token and TTL; integrate KMS for Private. 3) SDKs: add helpers to reconstruct fragments, surface soft-fail envelopes, and expose deferred call APIs. 4) Console: dashboard panels for tool_call success/failure rates and checkpoint latency. 5) Telemetry: define dimension names and expose to metrics pipeline.
References: runtime design doc (confluence), storage schema proposal (eng RFC), SDK surface sketch (drive).
test_plan:
- Unit: parsing/validation of schema-offer and fragment headers
- Integration: streaming session tests that inject dropped fragments and verify resumption via checkpoints
- Failure modes: simulate tool errors (500, 429, timeouts) and verify exponential retry + soft-fail envelope produced
- Idempotency: replay tool-call with same idempotency_token and ensure single side-effect
- Security: verify deferred payload encrypted at rest and access-controlled in Private setup
- Load: synthetic workload to validate checkpointing overhead at 5000 concurrent streams
- Regression: confirm older clients without schema-offer still receive best-effort frames and no data loss on happy path
qa_steps: 1) Deploy runtime feature-flag to staging. 2) Run e2e suite (integration + failure-mode tests). 3) Validate metrics pipeline shows expected counters. 4) Manual exploratory: start interactive client, force tool timeouts, confirm soft-fail envelope and suggested remediation shown. 5) Confirm encryption of deferred intents via KMS logs in Private environment.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1: behind feature flag in staging and internal canary (10% traffic on hosted). Monitor tool_call_failed_{class} and checkpoint_latency_ms for regressions.
- Phase 2: open to self-serve orgs on hosted as opt-in. Add console toggle 'Schema Governor Mode'.
- Phase 3: enable by default and offer migration guidance for Dedicated/Private customers (migration window 6 weeks).
- Emergency rollback: feature-flag off; operator playbook to purge pending deferred intents older than window and surface incident notes.
operator_playbook: 1) Alert: checkpoint_latency_ms > 2x baseline AND tool_call_failed_rate > 1% for 5m. 2) Triage: check runtime logs for schema_mismatch errors and inspect recent schema-offer frames. 3) If deferred-intent backlog growing: inspect DB queue, run 'drain-deferred' worker in dry-run to evaluate safe throughput. 4) For tool provider outages: change runtime policy to 'fail-fast' for non-critical tools and route critical tool calls to fallback implementations. 5) Post-incident: run the 'replay-and-validate' job against deferred-intent store to ensure idempotent replay into tool gateway. 6) Communications: use internal incident template to notify affected customers; include ETA and remediation steps.
